title: Uniform Circular Motion
body:
**Uniform circular motion** is travel around a circle at constant speed. It is accelerated
motion, because velocity is a [[Vector]] and its direction changes continuously even while its
magnitude does not.

The acceleration points toward the centre and has magnitude

$$
a = \frac{v^2}{r}
$$

so a car at 10 m/s on a curve of radius 5 m accelerates at $20\ \text{m/s}^2$, twice gravity.
Doubling the speed quadruples the acceleration, which is why a corner taken twice as fast needs
four times the grip.

That acceleration needs a net force to produce it, by [[Newton's Laws]], and the force is
supplied by something real in every case: [[Friction]] for a car, [[Tension]] for a ball on a
string, gravity for an orbit. There is no separate outward force acting on the object. The
outward feeling in a turning car is the passenger continuing in a straight line while the car
turns underneath them, which is the first law at work and requires no outward force at all.
